clue.text: One's embarrassed to involve woman in smear

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the smear word wraps round the woman

parts.note: to smear or smudge something is to blur it
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone is mortified at having to drag a woman into a smear campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as 'one is', so the definition describes the person who goes red.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reddens easily from shame or shyness is called by this noun, so it describes someone embarrassed.

clue.text: Strong drink makes bishop up for it

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
up for it means keen for sex, as is randy

explanation.surface: A spirit makes a bishop feel game for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up for it' is British slang for eager, often sexually; randy means lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from wine is a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Abandoned by commandos, comes back to life perhaps

definitions.meaning: going commando is slang for wearing no underwear, so commandos have abandoned their knickers and pants
a whimsical verb: to un-die is to reverse dying, as one returning to life does

explanation.surface: Soldiers leave behind something that revives.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are cryptic: 'going commando' means wearing nothing underneath, and the word split as UN-DIES means stops being dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for underwear, which the commando-goer leaves off, and also a mock verb for being raised from death.

clue.text: Goes drinking and nearly scores

definitions.meaning: to go to the pub to drink, an informal phrase
in football, striking the crossbar comes close to a goal

explanation.surface: Someone heads out for a drink and almost pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for heading to the pub, and in football a shot off the crossbar that almost goes in.

clue.text: Remove dry pieces from red curry — they can repeat

indicators.note: remove tells us to take the named letters away from the words that follow

parts.note: the pieces of the word dry are its separate letters D, R and Y

explanation.surface: Take the dry bits out of a red curry, as curries tend to repeat on you.
explanation.walkthrough: D, R and Y come out of RED CURRY one by one, leaving the answer. 'they can' just links: the curry repeating on you is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round again or happen once more, as indigestion does after a spicy meal.

clue.text: Eccentric involved in defending battleships

indicators.note: the letters are involved in, or tucked inside, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A crackpot has a hand in the defence of a naval fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals letters lying across the gap in 'defenDING BATtleships'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for a crazy or oddball person, the kind of eccentric whose behaviour is baffling.

clue.text: French philosopher who thought SS created mayhem

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A French thinker believed the Nazi SS caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mayhem' rearranges SS CREATED. 'who thought' nods to his 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: René of 'Cogito, ergo sum' fame is the French philosopher most famous for thinking.

clue.text: Animal conservationist starting national organisation against hunting …

indicators.note: starting points to the starting letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A wildlife campaigner launches a national anti-hunting group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes the initials of national organisation against hunting. The ellipsis runs the surface on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's ark-builder saved every animal species from the Flood, a conservationist of sorts.

clue.text: … introduces British group with pride, perhaps

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of spies or dealers
pride is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of a sin

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues: the anti-hunting group recruits a British pride of lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like a lions' group, but it is a deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for bringing forward or launching something new, such as a law or a recruit.

clue.text: Weird one tucked into end bits found on little piggies?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are tucked into the word for end bits

parts.note: tails are the end bits of animals

indicators.note: weird means strange, so these letters come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Curly tails on piglets have something odd tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy', played on a child's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the toe-counting nursery rhyme each little piggy is a toe, and the nails grow on them.

clue.text: Verification is essential to clause ceding title

indicators.note: the essential part of each word is its heart, so the central letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A contract checker insists a clause giving up someone's title is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential to' picks the middle letters: AU from clause, DI from ceding and T from title.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts or records checks and confirms that they are accurate.

clue.text: Abandoned area separating two sets of players

indicators.note: the area letter comes between the two groups of players, keeping them apart

parts.note: a cast is one set of players (actors) and a side another (a team)

explanation.surface: An empty patch of ground lies between two teams.
explanation.walkthrough: A cast is the company of actors in a play; a side is a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown away or rejected as no longer wanted has been discarded, deserted or abandoned.

clue.text: Red hot tape turned out to be highly informative porn!

indicators.note: turned out here means produced in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steamy tape turns out to be an explicit, very revealing blue movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges the letters of RED HOT TAPE. The definition plays on both senses: the 1972 porn film, and the code name of the Watergate informant who leaked to the Washington Post.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a notorious adult film and was borrowed for the secret source in the Watergate scandal, the most famous informer of all.

clue.text: City that can be stimulating after six

indicators.note: the city's name is what comes after the Roman six in the stimulating drug, so that front part is removed

parts.note: Viagra is the drug famous for its stimulating effect
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A city can be exciting once you get past six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the city, coming after six, is the stimulating pill: the solver strips the Roman numeral from the brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian city in Uttar Pradesh, best known as the home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Unwilling republican intervenes between countries

indicators.note: the republican letter comes between other letters, intervening inside the word

parts.note: intestate means without a will, a pun on unwilling

explanation.surface: A reluctant Republican politician steps into an international dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwilling' means reluctant on the surface but is read as un-will-ing, having made no will: INTESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for something linking or running between states, as US highways do; states are countries here.

clue.text: Worry about being disturbed as taxi lets gent in

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled when a cab lets a man climb in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges all sixteen letters of AS TAXI LETS GENT IN; 'lets ... in' looks like an insertion signal but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the dread or anxiety felt about the meaning of existence, worrying about one's very being.

clue.text: It shows popular autocrat taking first time off

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: taking, together with off, means the letter is removed
off completes the instruction to remove, here the first of two time letters

parts.note: a dictator is an autocrat

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word time, its usual one-letter abbreviation

explanation.surface: A well-liked tyrant shows himself taking his first holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... off' drops the first of the two Ts in DICTATOR, giving DICATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge or pointer is something that shows a reading, a level or a direction.

clue.text: Poet composed sonnet about New York

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about, or around, the city's abbreviation
composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A poet wrote a sonnet on New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges SONNET to TEN..SON, which goes 'about' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord of 'The Charge of the Light Brigade', was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: In the end, brings together seat majority

parts.note: the rear is one's seat or bottom
most means the majority

explanation.surface: Ultimately the seat majority is brought together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' sounds parliamentary alongside 'majority' but is the backside, REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for whatever is furthest back, the last in line at the very end.

clue.text: Stone passage reportedly found in Europe

parts.note: an emerald is a precious green stone

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the passage word is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A precious stone in a corridor is found somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: AISLE spoken sounds like ISLE. The definition is deliberately vague: Ireland, the poetic Emerald Isle, is something found in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic nickname for Ireland, a European country famed for its green landscape.

clue.text: Voltaire, ridiculing error, gutted church official

indicators.note: gutted means emptied of insides, so only the outside letters of each word survive

explanation.surface: Voltaire, mocking a mistake, demolished a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves VE from Voltaire, RG from ridiculing and ER from error.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay officer who looks after a church's interior and leads processions, carrying a rod.

clue.text: It helps to heal and keeps you from running

definitions.meaning: a surgical suture closes a wound so it can mend
a sharp pain in the side that stops a runner

explanation.surface: Something aids recovery and keeps you off the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a suture closing a wound and a sudden cramp in the side that halts runners.

clue.text: Nettle or grass?

definitions.meaning: to nettle is to annoy or irritate, a sense of this British slang verb
in British slang a grass is a police informer, and this word is another such name

explanation.surface: Is the plant a stinging weed or ordinary lawn grass?
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for both irritating someone and for an informer who tips off the police.

clue.text: Record film music first

indicators.note: first places the music word ahead of the film word

parts.note: a score is the music written for a film or show
a sheet is a thin layer or film, as of ice

explanation.surface: A soundtrack recording is made before the film itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like the cinema, but here it is a thin layer, SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: The card on which points or runs are written down is the record of a game.

clue.text: Criticism of missing copy

indicators.note: missing says the small word is absent from the longer one

parts.note: a reproof is a rebuke or criticism

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a copy has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes OF out of REPROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for reproduction, an imitation or replica of an original.

clue.text: It blows up in Estonia occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something explodes in Estonia every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of Estonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily's active volcano erupts from time to time, so it is something that blows up.

clue.text: Baseball player's casual clothing combination

parts.note: shorts are casual clothing
a combination outfit pairs the shorts with a top, the garment that completes it

explanation.surface: A ballplayer's off-duty outfit is a matching set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual clothing combination' gives two garments, SHORTS and a TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder positioned between second and third base in baseball holds this position.

clue.text: See 14
Against the rules to have one buried in the neighbourhood

indicators.note: the single letter is buried inside the phrase meaning close by

parts.note: something in the neighbourhood is not far away
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It's wrong to bury someone in the local area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' puts I inside NOT FAR, giving NOT FA-I-R.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust or unsporting conduct breaks the rules of fair play, the cry of a child cheated at a game.

clue.text: Close and terribly hot around where we live

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the word for close
terribly signals the letters are badly arranged

parts.note: near means close

explanation.surface: It's humid and very hot in the place we call home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like muggy weather beside 'hot', but means near.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans live on this planet, so the phrase locating us on the world says where we live.
